$comment: Conformance cases for `bolt-apps verify` (YAML and script layout level). Each case edits the base app and names the finding codes verify must report. `bolt_error_contains` is the text Bolt's own parser puts in the load error shown under Settings, Desktop App, User Apps, so a launcher-side test can run the same cases through the real parser: the expected result there is Err containing that text, or Ok when expect is empty. Cases without bolt_error_contains are checked by the toolkit only (the launcher text is not recorded yet).

base.utilities/eagle-info.yaml:
schema_version: 1
runtime: bridge
id: eagle-info
chip: eagle-info
title: "Eagle info"
emits: Generic
args:
  - { name: view, from: "query.word(0)", default: overview }
bridge:
  command:
    macos: "python3 {{scripts_dir}}/eagle-info__eagle.py {{view}}"
  parse: json
  timeout_seconds: 20
presentation:
  widget: list
  title_field: title

cases.name: chip differs from id: Bolt offers the app in the launcher but never runs it (the launcher looks apps up by id)
script run directly without a shebang
script named in the app is not in the pack
script in a folder under the app's own name (Bolt installs nested folders; every file is keyed by its full path)

script not named for the app: Bolt keeps every app's scripts in one shared folder, so a bare config.json or bolt_app_kit.py makes a second app fail with the Bolt error owned_by_other. That Bolt error needs two installed packs, so it cannot be a single-pack case here: bolt_error_contains does not apply, and the toolkit's own code is the check
script with a space in its name
emits a kind Bolt does not know
bridge runtime without a bridge block
